title: OHC: Opportunity-Constraint Heatmap — roadmap allocator for capacity-aware prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce the Opportunity-Constraint Heatmap (OHC), a hybrid prioritization model that overlays RICE-like opportunity scores with an explicit capacity constraint curve. Purpose: help PMs allocate finite Dedicated/Private rollout slots and engineering cycles while balancing token-cost and latency impact. OHC produces a ranked allocation and a recommended release bucket (canary, reserved, deferred) for initiatives based on scenario-aware capacity envelopes.
acceptance_criteria: Spreadsheet prototype with sample initiatives and inputs (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) that calculates OHC score and capacity-penalty adjusted ranking
Backtest: run OHC on last 12 months of initiatives and show >10% better alignment with token-cost budget constraints than naive RICE ordering
Visualization: roadmap heatmap tile in Notion/Productboard and an exported PNG for leadership review
Integration doc: one-page RFC describing inputs, how to interpret the constraint curve, and mapping to release buckets (canary/dedicated/defer)
notes: Motivation: teams currently use RICE variants but ignore capacity ceilings and latency-sensitive cost externalities; that causes expensive launches that blow monthly Dedicated commitments.

Core idea: compute base_opportunity = f(Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) then apply capacity_penalty = sigmoid((expected_tokens_per_minute - capacity_threshold) / scale) to reduce priority for high-cost items when capacity is scarce.
We will support two modes: operational (token/throughput constrained) and latency-sensitive (SLO-weighted).
Trade-offs: penalizing high-cost features may hide long-term strategic bets; mitigation is to expose an adjustable strategic_multiplier to override penalty for up to 2 initiatives per cycle.
Success metrics: fewer mid-cycle capacity breaches, adoption by 3 product teams in first two cycles, and improved token-cost forecast accuracy within 12%.
Non-goal: this does not replace qualitative prioritization; it's a decision support artifact to surface capacity-aware tradeoffs.
